claim: Phospho-proteomic studies of the fission yeast S. pombe have revealed a conserved phosphoserine residue that is located within the IQ-motif-containing neck region of class I and V myosins.
source: Phospho-proteomic studies of the fission yeast S. pombe (Carpy et al., 2014; Wilson-Grady et al., 2008) have revealed a conserved phosphoserine residue that is located within the IQ-motif-containing neck region of class I and V myosins (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published phospho-proteomic studies (Carpy et al., 2014; Wilson-Grady et al., 2008).

claim: The conserved phosphoserine residue is located at an AGC family kinase consensus phosphoserine site.
source: The location of this AGC family kinase consensus phosphoserine site (Pearce et al., 2010) has the potential to impact myosin activity and function by affecting light-chain binding and the conformation of the lever arm.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pearce et al., 2010, which defines AGC kinase consensus sites.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation was significantly reduced in cells lacking Ste20.
source: Myo1S742 phosphorylation was significantly reduced in cells lacking Ste20 (the fission yeast homolog of the core TORC2 component, RICTOR), and abolished in cells lacking the downstream AGC kinase, Gad8.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, which shows western blots comparing phosphorylation levels in different genetic backgrounds.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation was abolished in cells lacking the downstream AGC kinase, Gad8.
source: Myo1S742 phosphorylation was significantly reduced in cells lacking Ste20 (the fission yeast homolog of the core TORC2 component, RICTOR), and abolished in cells lacking the downstream AGC kinase, Gad8.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, which demonstrates no detectable phosphorylation in gad8∆ cells.

claim: Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in a TORC2–Gad8-kinase-dependent manner.
source: Thus, Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in a TORC2–Gad8-kinase-dependent manner (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1B showing reduced/abolished phosphorylation in TORC2 and Gad8 mutants.

claim: Gad8 kinase activity is reduced through the phosphorylation of a conserved threonine (T6) residue.
source: Within cells, Gad8 kinase activity is reduced through the phosphorylation of a conserved threonine (T6) residue (Du et al., 2016; Hálová et al., 2013) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Du et al., 2016 and Hálová et al., 2013.

claim: A significant reduction of Myo1S742 phosphorylation was observed in cells expressing phospho-mimetic Gad8.T6D.
source: A significant reduction of Myo1S742 phosphorylation was observed in cells expressing phospho-mimetic Gad8.T6D (Figure 1D), which has reduced Gad8 kinase activity (Du et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and a citation to Du et al., 2016.

claim: Gad8.T6D has reduced Gad8 kinase activity.
source: A significant reduction of Myo1S742 phosphorylation was observed in cells expressing phospho-mimetic Gad8.T6D (Figure 1D), which has reduced Gad8 kinase activity (Du et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Du et al., 2016.

claim: Schizosaccharomyces pombe cells lacking either TORC2 or Gad8 display defects in actin organization, polarized growth regulation and the control of cell-cycle progression.
source: Schizosaccharomyces pombe cells lacking either TORC2 or Gad8 display defects in actin organization, polarized growth regulation and the control of cell-cycle progression (Petersen and Nurse, 2007; Du et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Petersen and Nurse, 2007 and Du et al., 2016.

claim: Replacing Myo1 serine 742 with a phosphorylation-resistant alanine residue in myo1.S742A cells blocked the division of cells that were cultured for an extended period in restricted-growth medium.
source: Similarly, replacing Myo1 serine 742 with a phosphorylation-resistant alanine residue in myo1.S742A cells blocked the division of cells that were cultured for an extended period in restricted-growth medium (mean length ± SEM (µm): 6.67 ± 0.3 for wildtype cells; 18.50 ± 1.3 for myo1.S742A cells (n > 300)) (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing cell length measurements and images in Figure 1E.

claim: TORC2-directed Gad8-dependent phosphorylation at S742 regulates Myo1 activity.
source: We conclude that TORC2-directed Gad8-dependent phosphorylation at S742 regulates Myo1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the preceding paragraphs.

claim: Ca2+ binding induced a change in Cam1 conformation.
source: Together these probes demonstrated that Ca2+ binding induced a change in Cam1 conformation.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from FRET and IAANS fluorescence measurements described in the preceding text.

claim: The rate of Ca2+ ion release from Cam1 exhibited three phases, fast, medium and slow, of approximately equal amplitude with rate constants 137, 12.9 and 2.0 s−1, respectively.
source: The time-course of Ca2+ ion release exhibited three phases, fast, medium and slow, of approximately equal amplitude (rate constants 137, 12.9 and 2.0 s−1, respectively), indicating that the cation has different affinities for each Ca2+ binding lobe of Cam1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D measuring Ca2+ release kinetics.

claim: Cam1 binding to the IQ motif(s) stabilizes the α-helix and results in a drop in FRET signal in the absence of calcium.
source: Cam1 binding to the IQ motif(s) stabilizes the α-helix and results in a drop in FRET signal in the absence of calcium (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental FRET data shown in Figures 2E-G.

claim: Analysis of interactions between Cam1 and Myo1IQ12–FRET revealed two distinct phases to the association of Cam1 molecules with the combined Myo1IQ12 motifs.
source: Analysis of interactions between Cam1 and Myo1IQ12–FRET revealed two distinct phases to the association of Cam1 molecules with the combined Myo1IQ12 motifs. Each phase contributed 50% of the overall change in signal (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental FRET data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The first Cam1–Myo1IQ12-binding event corresponded to an affinity of less than 0.1 µM.
source: The first Cam1–Myo1IQ12-binding event corresponded to an affinity of less than 0.1 µM (binding was too tight to calculate affinity with higher precision), whereas the second event correlated with an approximately 10-fold weaker binding affinity (0.68 µM).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of experimental binding data.

claim: The second Cam1–Myo1IQ12-binding event correlated with an approximately 10-fold weaker binding affinity (0.68 µM).
source: The first Cam1–Myo1IQ12-binding event corresponded to an affinity of less than 0.1 µM (binding was too tight to calculate affinity with higher precision), whereas the second event correlated with an approximately 10-fold weaker binding affinity (0.68 µM).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of experimental binding data.

claim: Cam1 association with Myo1IQ12 was sensitive to calcium with a pCa of 5.87.
source: This association was sensitive to calcium (pCa of 5.87) (Figure 2C), indicating that Cam1 can only associate with both Myo1 IQ motifs at low cellular Ca2+ concentrations.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cam1 can only associate with both Myo1 IQ motifs at low cellular Ca2+ concentrations.
source: This association was sensitive to calcium (pCa of 5.87) (Figure 2C), indicating that Cam1 can only associate with both Myo1 IQ motifs at low cellular Ca2+ concentrations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the calcium sensitivity data.

claim: Cam1 bound tightly to a single, isolated, Myo1IQ1 alone with Kd <0.1 µM.
source: Interestingly, while Cam1 bound tightly to a single, isolated, Myo1IQ1 alone (Kd <0.1 µM), no detectable association was observed for the equivalent single Myo1IQ2 motif (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No detectable association was observed between Cam1 and the equivalent single Myo1IQ2 motif.
source: Interestingly, while Cam1 bound tightly to a single, isolated, Myo1IQ1 alone (Kd <0.1 µM), no detectable association was observed for the equivalent single Myo1IQ2 motif (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The stable residency of Cam1 in the first IQ position is required before calmodulin can bind to Myo1IQ2.
source: Together these data are consistent with a sequential cooperative binding mechanism in which the stable residency of Cam1 in the first IQ position is required before calmodulin can bind to Myo1IQ2.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the binding data showing differential affinities for IQ1 vs IQ2.

claim: Replacing serine 742 with a phosphomimetic aspartic acid residue had no significant impact upon the affinity, calcium sensitivity or cooperative nature of the interaction between Myo1 and Cam1.
source: Replacing serine 742 within the IQ neck region with a phosphomimetic aspartic acid residue had no significant impact upon the affinity, calcium sensitivity or cooperative nature of the interaction between Myo1 and Cam1 (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The S742D replacement resulted in a change in maximum FRET signal upon Cam1 binding (Fmax 46.05 vs 31.64).
source: However, the S742D replacement resulted in a change in maximum FRET signal upon Cam1 binding (Fmax 46.05 vs 31.64) (Figure 2F), indicating that Myo1S742 phosphorylation changes the conformation of the lever arm upon Cam1 binding, rather than modulating the affinity of the neck region for Cam1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental FRET data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation changes the conformation of the lever arm upon Cam1 binding, rather than modulating the affinity of the neck region for Cam1.
source: However, the S742D replacement resulted in a change in maximum FRET signal upon Cam1 binding (Fmax 46.05 vs 31.64) (Figure 2F), indicating that Myo1S742 phosphorylation changes the conformation of the lever arm upon Cam1 binding, rather than modulating the affinity of the neck region for Cam1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FRET data showing conformational changes without affinity changes.

claim: Immunofluorescence using Myo1S742 phospho-specific antibodies confirmed the presence of serine-742 phosphorylated Myo1 at cortical foci.
source: Immunofluorescence using Myo1S742 phospho-specific antibodies confirmed the presence of serine-742 phosphorylated Myo1 at cortical foci (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Myo1 and Cam1 associated with the cell membrane in two distinct ways: rapid, transient, binding of single Myo1 molecules to the cell membrane, and longer endocytic events.
source: Myo1 and Cam1 associated with the cell membrane in two distinct ways: we observed both (i) rapid, transient, binding of single Myo1 molecules to the cell membrane, characterized by low-intensity, single, stepwise, changes in intensity (Video 1), alongside (ii) longer endocytic events that were much brighter and took much longer (Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by TIRF imaging data shown in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: The rapid, single-molecule, interactions of Myo1 and Cam1 with the membrane had low mobility (0.03 µm2.s−1).
source: The rapid, single-molecule, interactions of Myo1 and Cam1 with the membrane had low mobility (0.03 µm2.s−1), ~10 times slower than the diffusion of integral membrane proteins (Mashanov et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental mobility measurements and comparison to published data (Mashanov et al., 2010).

claim: The durations of short single-molecule events were exponentially distributed with mean lifetime of ~8 s−1.
source: The durations of these short single-molecule events (defined as the period over which individual objects were observed and their paths tracked) were exponentially distributed with mean lifetime of ~8 s−1 (n = 152) (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental tracking data from Video 1.

claim: During endocytic events, the fluorescence signal increased gradually at a rate corresponding to ~13 molecules.s−1 to a peak amplitude corresponding to ~45 molecules of mNeongreen.Myo1.
source: By contrast, during endocytic events, the fluorescence signal increased gradually (at a rate corresponding to ~13 molecules.s−1) to a peak amplitude corresponding to ~45 molecules of mNeongreen.Myo1, which persisted for ~6 s (plateau phase), before decaying back to baseline level (at a rate of ~14 molecules.s−1) (Figure 3B, Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: The duration (Tdur) of endocytic events was 13.84 s ± 0.39 (mean ± SEM, n = 50).
source: The duration (Tdur) of endocytic events (measured as described in the Materials and methods) was 13.84 s ± 0.39 (mean ± SEM, n = 50) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Tdur was significantly shorter for Cam1.GFP (10.99 s +/– 0.21, n = 52) compared to mNeongreen.Myo1 (p<0.0001).
source: To explore how this phosphorylation affected Myo1 and calmodulin dynamics in vivo, we generated prototroph S. pombe strains in which endogenous myo1, cam1, or cam2 genes were fused to cDNA encoding monomeric fluorescent proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Using high-speed (20 fps) single-molecule total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) imaging, we explored how Myo1S742 phosphorylation impacts Myo1 and Cam1 dynamics and function in vivo. Myo1 and Cam1 associated with the cell membrane in two distinct ways: we observed both (i) rapid, transient, binding of single Myo1 molecules to the cell membrane, characterized by low-intensity, single, stepwise, changes in intensity (Video 1), alongside (ii) longer endocytic events that were much brighter and took much longer (Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements comparing Cam1 and Myo1 dynamics.

claim: The peak (plateau) intensity for Cam1.GFP was roughly double that measured for mNeongreen.Myo1 and equivalent to ~90 GFP molecules.
source: The fluorescence intensity dynamics of Cam1.GFP during endocytic events were similar to those of mNeongreen.Myo1, but Tdur was significantly shorter for Cam1.GFP (p<0.0001), 10.99 s +/– 0.21 (n = 52) while the peak (plateau) intensity for Cam1.GFP was roughly double that measured for mNeongreen.Myo1 and equivalent to ~90 GFP molecules (Figure 3C), consistent with the occupation of both IQ sites within the Myo1 neck region by Cam1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental intensity measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The peak intensity for Cam1.GFP is consistent with the occupation of both IQ sites within the Myo1 neck region by Cam1.
source: The fluorescence intensity dynamics of Cam1.GFP during endocytic events were similar to those of mNeongreen.Myo1, but Tdur was significantly shorter for Cam1.GFP (p<0.0001), 10.99 s +/– 0.21 (n = 52) while the peak (plateau) intensity for Cam1.GFP was roughly double that measured for mNeongreen.Myo1 and equivalent to ~90 GFP molecules (Figure 3C), consistent with the occupation of both IQ sites within the Myo1 neck region by Cam1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the stoichiometry of fluorescence intensity measurements.

claim: Cam1 dissociates from Myo1 before Myo1 leaves the endocytic patch.
source: The briefer event duration observed for Cam1 is best explained by the dissociation of Cam1 from Myo1 before Myo1 leaves the endocytic patch.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the timing differences between Cam1 and Myo1 dynamics.

claim: Two-color imaging of mNeongreen.myo1 cam1.mCherry cells revealed that Myo1 and Cam1 arrived simultaneously at the endocytic patch, before Cam1.mCherry disassociated ~3 s before mNeongreen.Myo1.
source: This process was confirmed by two-color imaging of mNeongreen.myo1 cam1.mCherry cells, which revealed how Myo1 and Cam1 arrived simultaneously at the endocytic patch, before Cam1.mCherry disassociated ~3 s before mNeongreen.Myo1 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by two-color TIRF imaging data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The duration of the signal (Tdur) was 1.5 s shorter for Myo1S742A (12.3 s + /- 0.31 n = 67) compared to wild-type Myo1.
source: Myo1 and Cam1 dynamics in myo1.S742A cells during endocytosis revealed how Myo1S742A had average assembly and disassembly rates and peak intensity measurements that were identical to those of wild-type Myo1, yet the duration of the signal (Tdur) was 1.5 s shorter for Myo1S742A (12.3 s + /- 0.31 n = 67) (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Myo1S742A and Cam1 proteins disassociated simultaneously and somewhat earlier during the endocytic event than in otherwise isogenic wild-type cells.
source: However, Myo1S742A and Cam1 proteins disassociated simultaneously and somewhat earlier during the endocytic event than in otherwise isogenic wild-type cells.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of timing data between wild-type and mutant cells.

claim: Upon cell division, fission yeast cells grow exclusively from the old cell end that existed in the parental cell.
source: Upon cell division, fission yeast cells grow exclusively from the old cell end that existed in the parental cell. At a point during interphase (called New End Take Off (NETO)), there is a transition to bipolar growth (Mitchison and Nurse, 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mitchison and Nurse, 1985.

claim: At a point during interphase (called New End Take Off (NETO)), there is a transition to bipolar growth.
source: Upon cell division, fission yeast cells grow exclusively from the old cell end that existed in the parental cell. At a point during interphase (called New End Take Off (NETO)), there is a transition to bipolar growth (Mitchison and Nurse, 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mitchison and Nurse, 1985.

claim: The cell-cycle switch in growth pattern correlates precisely with a parallel redistribution of endocytic actin patches.
source: This cell-cycle switch in growth pattern correlates precisely with a parallel redistribution of endocytic actin patches (Marks and Hyams, 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Marks and Hyams, 1985.

claim: The lifetimes of Myo1 and Cam1 foci were shorter in myo1.S742A cells than in myo1+ cells.
source: The TIRF imaging data were consistent with widefield, 3D, time-lapse imaging that showed that the lifetimes of Myo1 and Cam1 foci were shorter in myo1.S742A cells than in myo1+ cells (Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data referenced in Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: The myo1.S742A allele did not affect the accumulation of Cam2 or LifeACT at sites of endocytosis.
source: By contrast, while the myo1.S742A allele did not affect the accumulation of Cam2 or LifeACT at sites of endocytosis (Supplementary file 1 Table 1), the rate of endocytosis (as measured by actin foci lifetimes) differed significantly (p<0.01) between the old and new ends of myo1-S742A cells but not of wild-type cells (lifetimes at old end and new cell end: 11.96 ± 2.28 and 11.39 ± 1.07 for wild-type cells; 14.17 ± 3.3 and 11.09 ± 1.29 s for myo1.S742A cells (mean ± s.d.)).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: The rate of endocytosis (as measured by actin foci lifetimes) differed significantly (p<0.01) between the old and new ends of myo1-S742A cells but not of wild-type cells.
source: By contrast, while the myo1.S742A allele did not affect the accumulation of Cam2 or LifeACT at sites of endocytosis (Supplementary file 1 Table 1), the rate of endocytosis (as measured by actin foci lifetimes) differed significantly (p<0.01) between the old and new ends of myo1-S742A cells but not of wild-type cells (lifetimes at old end and new cell end: 11.96 ± 2.28 and 11.39 ± 1.07 for wild-type cells; 14.17 ± 3.3 and 11.09 ± 1.29 s for myo1.S742A cells (mean ± s.d.)).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of actin foci lifetimes.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation does not impact the assembly of Myo1–Cam1 endocytic foci.
source: Therefore, although Myo1S742 phosphorylation does not impact the assembly of Myo1–Cam1 endocytic foci, it regulates myosin-1 to modulate the activity and function of the ensemble of endocytic proteins during bipolar growth.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing no change in assembly but changes in function.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation regulates myosin-1 to modulate the activity and function of the ensemble of endocytic proteins during bipolar growth.
source: Therefore, although Myo1S742 phosphorylation does not impact the assembly of Myo1–Cam1 endocytic foci, it regulates myosin-1 to modulate the activity and function of the ensemble of endocytic proteins during bipolar growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on endocytosis rates and timing.

claim: Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in a cell-cycle-dependent manner.
source: Analysis of extracts from cell-division cycle mutants arrested in G1 (cdc10.v50 cells) prior to NETO (Marks et al., 1986) or in late G2 (cdc25.22 cells) after NETO revealed that Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in a cell-cycle-dependent manner (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental western blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: At its peak in early interphase (prior to the transition to a bipolar growth pattern), approximately half of cellular Myo1 is phosphorylated on S742.
source: These data established that, at its peak in early interphase (prior to the transition to a bipolar growth pattern), approximately half of cellular Myo1 is phosphorylated on S742, before dropping to undetectable levels by the end of late G2 (the Cdc25 execution point), prior to entry into mitosis.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of cell-cycle synchronized western blot data.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation drops to undetectable levels by the end of late G2 (the Cdc25 execution point), prior to entry into mitosis.
source: These data established that, at its peak in early interphase (prior to the transition to a bipolar growth pattern), approximately half of cellular Myo1 is phosphorylated on S742, before dropping to undetectable levels by the end of late G2 (the Cdc25 execution point), prior to entry into mitosis.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of cell-cycle synchronized western blot data.

claim: myo1.S742A cells have a longer average length than wild-type cells (9.77 ± 1.77 µm for myo1+; 13.2 ± 2.47 µm for myo1.S742A; t-test >99% significance; n > 500).
source: myo1.S742A cells have a longer average length than wild-type cells ( 9.77 ± 1.77 µm for myo1+; 13.2 ± 2.47 µm for myo1.S742A; t-test >99% significance; n > 500).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental cell length measurements.

claim: 24.7% of myo1.S742A cells developed a bent morphology (i.e. growth deviates by >5° from the longitudinal axis).
source: In addition to the NETO phenotype, a significant proportion of myo1.S742A cells exhibited significant issues with their ability to maintain, linear, polarized, growth, as 24.7% of these cells developed a bent morphology (i.e. growth deviates by >5° from the longitudinal axis) (Figure 4E-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental morphology analysis shown in Figures 4E-F.

claim: The myo1.S742A allele did not have an additive effect on the growth-polarity defects associated with cells lacking Tea4.
source: The myo1.S742A allele did not have an additive effect on the growth-polarity defects associated with cells lacking Tea4, a polarity determinant protein that plays an important role in integrating actin cytoskeleton function with the regulation of polarised cell growth (Martin et al., 2005; Tatebe et al., 2005) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental genetic interaction data shown in Figure 5A and citations to Martin et al., 2005 and Tatebe et al., 2005.

claim: A significantly higher than normal proportion of myo1.S742A cells exhibited monopolar growth when compared to equivalent wild type.
source: Consistently, cell-wall staining revealed a significantly higher than normal proportion of myo1.S742A cells that exhibited monopolar growth (when compared to equivalent wild type), indicating a disruption in the switch from monopolar to bipolar growth (Figure 4E-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental cell-wall staining data shown in Figures 4E-F.

claim: Sla2 failed to redistribute to the newly divided end of myo1.S742A cells during interphase.
source: This was confirmed by tracking the cellular distribution of the actin-patch marker, Sla2/End4, following cell division. Sla2 failed to redistribute to the newly divided end of myo1.S742A cells during interphase (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental tracking data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The failure of myo1.S742A cells to switch to bipolar growth is consistent with the reduced growth rate at the end of the log phase.
source: This failure of myo1.S742A cells to switch to bipolar growth, a and restrict growth upon nutrient depletion (Figure 1E) is consistent with the reduced growth rate at the end of the log phase and with growth to an overall higher density upon reaching the stationary phase (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on correlation of phenotypes observed in growth curve data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: myo1.S742A cells grow to an overall higher density upon reaching the stationary phase.
source: This failure of myo1.S742A cells to switch to bipolar growth, a and restrict growth upon nutrient depletion (Figure 1E) is consistent with the reduced growth rate at the end of the log phase and with growth to an overall higher density upon reaching the stationary phase (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental growth curve data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cell-cycle-dependent changes in Myo1S742 phosphorylation modulate the ability of the myosin lever arm region to regulate endocytosis and polarized growth.
source: We conclude that cell-cycle-dependent changes in Myo1S742 phosphorylation modulate the ability of the myosin lever arm region to regulate endocytosis and polarized growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on cell-cycle phosphorylation and growth phenotypes.

claim: Myo1 has been reported to associate with a second calmodulin-like protein, Cam2, via its second IQ motif.
source: Myo1 has been reported to associate with a second calmodulin-like protein, Cam2, via its second IQ motif (Sammons et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sammons et al., 2011.

claim: Cam1 occupies both Myo1 IQ motifs during endocytosis.
source: However, our data indicate that Cam1 occupies both Myo1 IQ motifs during endocytosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stoichiometry and binding data presented earlier.

claim: Myo1 and Cam1 dynamics at endocytic foci differ significantly from Cam2 dynamics at these foci.
source: Widefield microscopy revealed that Myo1 and Cam1 dynamics (Figure 6A) at endocytic foci differ significantly from Cam2 dynamics at these foci.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental widefield microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cam2 is recruited to sites of endocytosis later than Myo1 and Cam1, but prior to vesicle scission/budding.
source: Cam2 is recruited to sites of endocytosis later than Myo1 and Cam1, but prior to vesicle scission/budding, whereupon, like CAPZAAcp1, Sla2 and actin, Cam2 remains associated with laterally oscillating, internalized, endosomes (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figures 6B-C.

claim: Cam2 remains associated with laterally oscillating, internalized, endosomes after vesicle scission/budding.
source: Cam2 is recruited to sites of endocytosis later than Myo1 and Cam1, but prior to vesicle scission/budding, whereupon, like CAPZAAcp1, Sla2 and actin, Cam2 remains associated with laterally oscillating, internalized, endosomes (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figures 6B-C.

claim: Cam1 and Cam2 localize to a significant proportion of foci lacking the other calmodulin.
source: Similarly, simultaneous imaging of Cam1 and Cam2 in cam1.mCherry cam2.gfp cells revealed how each protein localizes to a significant proportion of foci lacking the other calmodulin, thereby highlighting the different timings of the engagement of each molecule with the endocytic machinery (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental two-color imaging data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cam1 recruitment to endocytic foci is abolished when Myo1 is absent.
source: Finally, although Cam1 recruitment to endocytic foci is abolished when Myo1 is absent (Figure 6E), the intensity, volume and number of Cam2 foci actually increases in the absence of Myo1 (Figure 6F Supplementary file 1 Table 1), even though the internalization and lateral 'oscillating' dynamics of Cam2 and actin were dependent on Myo1 (Figure 6F & G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The intensity, volume and number of Cam2 foci actually increases in the absence of Myo1.
source: Finally, although Cam1 recruitment to endocytic foci is abolished when Myo1 is absent (Figure 6E), the intensity, volume and number of Cam2 foci actually increases in the absence of Myo1 (Figure 6F Supplementary file 1 Table 1), even though the internalization and lateral 'oscillating' dynamics of Cam2 and actin were dependent on Myo1 (Figure 6F & G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figure 6F and Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: The internalization and lateral 'oscillating' dynamics of Cam2 and actin were dependent on Myo1.
source: Finally, although Cam1 recruitment to endocytic foci is abolished when Myo1 is absent (Figure 6E), the intensity, volume and number of Cam2 foci actually increases in the absence of Myo1 (Figure 6F Supplementary file 1 Table 1), even though the internalization and lateral 'oscillating' dynamics of Cam2 and actin were dependent on Myo1 (Figure 6F & G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: On average, a total of ~30 Cam2 molecules were recruited to each endocytic focus.
source: TIRF imaging revealed that, on average, a total of ~30 Cam2 molecules were recruited to each endocytic focus (compared to 45 and 90 molecules observed for Myo1 and Cam1, respectively), and that the kinetics of Cam2 recruitment to foci differed significantly to those observed for both Myo1 and Cam1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging measurements.

claim: The kinetics of Cam2 recruitment to foci differed significantly to those observed for both Myo1 and Cam1.
source: TIRF imaging revealed that, on average, a total of ~30 Cam2 molecules were recruited to each endocytic focus (compared to 45 and 90 molecules observed for Myo1 and Cam1, respectively), and that the kinetics of Cam2 recruitment to foci differed significantly to those observed for both Myo1 and Cam1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging data.

claim: The Cam2 signal often increased steadily, before an abrupt decline.
source: The Cam2 signal often increased steadily, before an abrupt decline (Figure 7A), which contrasts with the more gradual (sigmoidal) rise and decay in intensity observed for Myo1 and Cam1 (Figure 3C, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cam2 continued to be associated with the endocytic vesicles after they were internalized and their connection with the cell membrane was broken.
source: TIRF microscopy (TIRFM) confirmed that Cam2 continued to be associated with the endocytic vesicles after they were internalized and their connection with the cell membrane was broken (Video 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental TIRF imaging data shown in Video 3.

claim: Endosome scission takes place immediately prior to the Myo1 disassembly phase.
source: Therefore endosome scission takes place immediately prior to the Myo1 disassembly phase (Figure 3B), and around the time when Cam1 dissociates from Myo1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the timing data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: Endosome scission occurs around the time when Cam1 dissociates from Myo1.
source: Therefore endosome scission takes place immediately prior to the Myo1 disassembly phase (Figure 3B), and around the time when Cam1 dissociates from Myo1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the timing data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The overall distribution of Myo1 and Cam1 appeared to be unaffected in cam2∆ cells.
source: Intriguingly, although the overall distribution of Myo1 and Cam1 appeared to be unaffected in cam2∆ cells, the number, volume and intensity of foci were significantly reduced (Figure 7C, D; Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figures 7C-D and Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: The number, volume and intensity of Myo1 and Cam1 foci were significantly reduced in cam2∆ cells.
source: Intriguingly, although the overall distribution of Myo1 and Cam1 appeared to be unaffected in cam2∆ cells, the number, volume and intensity of foci were significantly reduced (Figure 7C, D; Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figures 7C-D and Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: Two Cam2 molecules can associate with the unphosphorylated Myo1IQ12 region.
source: In vitro analysis revealed how two Cam2 molecules can associate with the unphosphorylated Myo1IQ12 region (Figure 2F) in a process that has two distinct phases.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: For Cam2, 70% of the signal change was brought about by a single binding event, associated with an affinity of 1.10 µM.
source: In contrast to Cam1, in which the two Myo1IQ12 binding events contributed equally to the change in FRET signal, for Cam2, 70% of the signal change was brought about by a single binding event, associated with an affinity of 1.10 µM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data analysis.

claim: Cam2 failed to associate with calcium.
source: As predicted from sequence analysis, Cam2 failed to associate with calcium (Figure 2D), and its conformation and interactions with Myo1 were insensitive to the divalent cation (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cam2 conformation and interactions with Myo1 were insensitive to calcium.
source: As predicted from sequence analysis, Cam2 failed to associate with calcium (Figure 2D), and its conformation and interactions with Myo1 were insensitive to the divalent cation (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Cam2 had a higher affinity for the first IQ motif (0.4 µM) than for both IQ1 and IQ2 together.
source: Like Cam1, Cam2 had a higher affinity for the first IQ motif (0.4 µM) than for both IQ1 and IQ2 together, and failed to bind IQ2 alone (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Cam2 failed to bind IQ2 alone.
source: Like Cam1, Cam2 had a higher affinity for the first IQ motif (0.4 µM) than for both IQ1 and IQ2 together, and failed to bind IQ2 alone (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental binding data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Cam1 calcium binding was unaffected by Cam2.
source: Cam1 calcium binding, as measured by IAANS labeling or by change in Quin-2 fluorescence were unaffected by Cam2, whereas gel filtration and fluorescence binding assays provided no evidence of a direct physical interaction between the two proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Gel filtration and fluorescence binding assays provided no evidence of a direct physical interaction between Cam1 and Cam2.
source: Cam1 calcium binding, as measured by IAANS labeling or by change in Quin-2 fluorescence were unaffected by Cam2, whereas gel filtration and fluorescence binding assays provided no evidence of a direct physical interaction between the two proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A difference in fluorescence amplitudes between Cam1 and Cam2 binding to the IQ12 motif indicated an impact upon the conformation of the lever arm.
source: Interestingly, a difference in fluorescence amplitudes between Cam1 and Cam2 binding to the IQ12 motif indicated an impact upon the conformation of the lever arm (Figure 2G), providing a potential mechanism to control Myo1 motor activity directly.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental fluorescence data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation had no measurable impact upon the dynamics and distribution of Cam2 within S. pombe cells undergoing normal vegetative growth.
source: However, Myo1S742 phosphorylation had no measurable impact upon the dynamics and distribution of Cam2 within S. pombe cells undergoing normal vegetative growth (Figure 8A; Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figure 8A and Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: Calcium levels within log phase yeast cells are relatively low (100–200 nM).
source: Calcium levels within log phase yeast cells are relatively low (100–200 nM) (Ma et al., 2011; Miseta et al., 1999), and so provide conditions that favor the association of Cam1 with Myo1 (pCa, 5.87).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2011 and Miseta et al., 1999.

claim: The relative abundance of Myo1: Cam1: Cam2 within the S. pombe cell is 0.25: 1.56: 1.
source: Analysis of cell fluorescence indicated the relative abundance of Myo1: Cam1: Cam2 within the S. pombe cell to be 0.25: 1.56: 1 (Supplementary file 1 Table 1), which is similar to the ratio defined by quantitative proteomic analysis of 0.45: 1.56: 1 (Marguerat et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental fluorescence analysis in Supplementary file 1 Table 1 and comparison to published proteomic data (Marguerat et al., 2012).

claim: 1.7% of Cam1 associated with discrete foci within cells.
source: Similarly, image analysis of Cam1–GFP fluorescence showed how 1.7% of Cam1 associated with discrete foci within cells (Supplementary file 1 Table 1), 40% of which was dependent upon Myo1, with the majority associating with the SPB (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental image analysis in Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: 40% of Cam1 foci were dependent upon Myo1.
source: Similarly, image analysis of Cam1–GFP fluorescence showed how 1.7% of Cam1 associated with discrete foci within cells (Supplementary file 1 Table 1), 40% of which was dependent upon Myo1, with the majority associating with the SPB (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental image analysis and data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: ~0.68% of cellular Cam1 associates with Myo1 at dynamic endocytic foci.
source: This indicates that ~0.68% of cellular Cam1 associates with Myo1 at dynamic endocytic foci.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental data on Cam1 localization.

claim: Sporadic prolonged calcium bursts occur upon pheromone release during mating.
source: Although Ca2+ levels are low during vegetative growth, sporadic prolonged calcium bursts occur upon pheromone release during mating (Carbó et al., 2017; Iida et al., 1990), and levels elevate significantly (~10 fold) during the subsequent meiosis and sporulation (Suizu et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Carbó et al., 2017 and Iida et al., 1990.

claim: Calcium levels elevate significantly (~10 fold) during meiosis and sporulation.
source: Although Ca2+ levels are low during vegetative growth, sporadic prolonged calcium bursts occur upon pheromone release during mating (Carbó et al., 2017; Iida et al., 1990), and levels elevate significantly (~10 fold) during the subsequent meiosis and sporulation (Suizu et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Suizu et al., 1995.

claim: Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in mating and meiotic cells.
source: We observed that Myo1S742 is phosphorylated in mating and meiotic cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental western blot data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Cam2 abundance increases significantly in relation to Cam1 upon starvation, mating and entry into meiosis.
source: Cam2 abundance simultaneously increases significantly in relation to Cam1 upon starvation, mating and entry into meiosis (Mata and Bähler, 2006; Mata et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mata and Bähler, 2006 and Mata et al., 2002.

claim: The lifetimes and dynamics of Myo1, Cam1 and Cam2 foci differ significantly from those observed in vegetative cells (p<0.0001), with foci lasting significantly longer (>1 min) in meiotic and sporulating cells.
source: Consistent with this prediction, the lifetimes and dynamics of Myo1, Cam1 and Cam2 foci differ significantly from those observed in vegetative cells (p<0.0001), with foci lasting significantly longer (>1 min) in meiotic and sporulating cells (Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: In cells undergoing meiosis and subsequent spore formation, cortical foci containing accumulations of Cam2 and actin were less dynamic, lacking any oscillation and remaining in a fixed position, and had a significantly longer lifetime than foci within actively growing cells.
source: In contrast to vegetative cells, in cells undergoing meiosis and subsequent spore formation, cortical foci containing accumulations of Cam2 and actin (like those containing like Myo1 and Cam1) were less dynamic, lacking any oscillation and remaining in a fixed position, and had a significantly longer lifetime than foci within actively growing cells (Figure 8D, Supplementary file 1 Table 1, Videos 5–8).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental imaging data shown in Figure 8D, Supplementary file 1 Table 1, and Videos 5-8.

claim: Endocytosis is significantly diminished in fusing and meiotic cells.
source: Consistent with this, endocytosis is significantly diminished in fusing and meiotic cells (Figure 8E) containing the stable Myo1, Cam1, Cam2 or actin foci, indicating that the reduction in foci dynamics minimizes endocytosis in meiotic cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The reduction in foci dynamics minimizes endocytosis in meiotic cells.
source: Consistent with this, endocytosis is significantly diminished in fusing and meiotic cells (Figure 8E) containing the stable Myo1, Cam1, Cam2 or actin foci, indicating that the reduction in foci dynamics minimizes endocytosis in meiotic cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation between foci dynamics and endocytosis rates.

claim: The lifetime of Myo1 and Cam1 foci were not significantly different to each other in myo1.S742A cells during meiosis.
source: Finally, we used the myo1.S742A allele to monitor the impact of Myo1S742 phosphorylation on Myo1, Cam1 and Cam2 dynamics during meiosis. In contrast to wild-type cells, the lifetime of Myo1 and Cam1 foci were not significantly different to each other in myo1.S742A cells.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of foci lifetimes in wild-type vs mutant cells during meiosis.

claim: The lifetime of the Myo1 and Cam1 foci in myo1.S742A cells were significantly reduced when compared to those in the wild type during meiosis.
source: In addition, the lifetime of the Myo1 and Cam1 foci in myo1.S742A cells were significantly reduced when compared to those in the wild type.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison of foci lifetimes.

claim: Cam2 dynamics did not correlate with Myo1 in myo1.S742A cells during meiosis, which is in contrast to those in the wild type.
source: Cam2 dynamics did not correlate with Myo1 in myo1.S742A cells, which is in contrast to those in the wild type (Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: Myo1S742 phosphorylation is required for Cam2 to interact with the Myo1 IQ motif and thereby reduce Myo1 foci dynamics.
source: These data indicate that Myo1S742 phosphorylation is required for Cam2 to interact with the Myo1 IQ motif and thereby reduce Myo1 foci dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Cam2 dynamics in phosphorylation mutants.

claim: Heterothallic (h90) nitrogen-starved G1-arrested myo1.S742A cells failed to inhibit polar growth.
source: Consistent with observations of myo1.S742A cells grown to stationary phase (Figure 1E), heterothallic (h90) nitrogen-starved G1-arrested myo1.S742A cells failed to inhibit polar growth (Figure 8F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 8F.

claim: 27.9% of mating myo1.S742A cells continued to grow at their mating (schmooing) tips (vs 1.8% of myo1+ cells; n > 100).
source: 27.9% of mating myo1.S742A cells continued to grow at their mating (schmooing) tips (vs of myo1+ 1.8% cells; n > 100), and meioses frequently produced asci with an abnormal number of unequally sized spores (Figure 8F , arrowheads) ( 0.9% of myo1+ asci, 13.1% of myo1.S742A asci; n > 100).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental quantification shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Meioses in myo1.S742A cells frequently produced asci with an abnormal number of unequally sized spores (0.9% of myo1+ asci, 13.1% of myo1.S742A asci; n > 100).
source: 27.9% of mating myo1.S742A cells continued to grow at their mating (schmooing) tips (vs of myo1+ 1.8% cells; n > 100), and meioses frequently produced asci with an abnormal number of unequally sized spores (Figure 8F , arrowheads) ( 0.9% of myo1+ asci, 13.1% of myo1.S742A asci; n > 100).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental quantification shown in Figure 8F.

claim: The spore defect phenotype in myo1.S742A cells is reminiscent of the meiotic phenotype of cam2∆ cells.
source: This spore defect phenotype is reminiscent of the meiotic phenotype of cam2∆ cells (Itadani et al., 2006), which supports the view that increases in cellular Ca2+ and Myo1S742 phosphorylation are both key for Cam2 association with and regulation of Myo1.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison to published phenotypes (Itadani et al., 2006).

claim: Increases in cellular Ca2+ and Myo1S742 phosphorylation are both key for Cam2 association with and regulation of Myo1.
source: This spore defect phenotype is reminiscent of the meiotic phenotype of cam2∆ cells (Itadani et al., 2006), which supports the view that increases in cellular Ca2+ and Myo1S742 phosphorylation are both key for Cam2 association with and regulation of Myo1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phenotypic similarities and experimental data.

claim: Changes in calcium levels and TORC2-dependent phosphorylation status provides a two-stage mechanism for modulating motor activity.
source: These data support a model in which changes in calcium levels and TORC2-dependent phosphorylation status provides a simple two-stage mechanism for modulating motor activity.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Phosphorylation of the myosin heavy chain regulates light chain specificity, and lever arm conformation and flexibility, to impact upon cellular function.
source: Here, we describe a newly discovered mechanism through which phosphorylation of the myosin heavy chain (Figure 1) regulates light chain specificity, and lever arm conformation and flexibility, to impact upon cellular function.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented.

claim: During the vegetative life cycle, at basal levels of cellular calcium, S. pombe Myo1 preferentially associates with two molecules of the calcium-regulated calmodulin light-chain Cam1.
source: During the vegetative life cycle, at basal levels of cellular calcium, S. pombe Myo1 preferentially associates with two molecules of the calcium-regulated calmodulin light-chain Cam1 (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: During early stages of the cell cycle, phosphorylation of the Myo1 neck region changes the conformation of the Cam1-associated lever arm to moderate motor activity, thereby regulating the rate of endocytosis, and a switch from monopolar to bipolar growth.
source: During early stages of the cell cycle, phosphorylation of the Myo1 neck region (Figure 8G) changes the conformation of the Cam1-associated lever arm to moderate motor activity, thereby regulating the rate of endocytosis, and a switch from monopolar to bipolar growth (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figures 5 and 8G.

claim: There is a significant increase in TORC2 and Gad8 activity upon starvation, which promotes the onset of the meiotic lifecycle.
source: There is a significant increase in TORC2 and Gad8 activity upon starvation, which promotes the onset of the meiotic lifecycle (Hálová et al., 2013; Laboucarié et al., 2017; Martín et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hálová et al., 2013, Laboucarié et al., 2017, and Martín et al., 2017.

claim: Upon starvation, there is an increase in Myo1 serine 472 phosphorylation.
source: Upon starvation, there is an increase in Myo1 serine 472 phosphorylation (Figure 8), and myo1.S742A cells fail to arrest growth in response to starvation (Figures 1E and Figure 8F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Phosphorylation of the IQ region, combined with an increase in cytosolic Ca2+ levels observed during G1, starvation and meiosis, switches light chain preference to favor the recruitment of a single molecule of the calcium-insensitive calmodulin-like Cam2.
source: Phosphorylation of the IQ region, combined with an increase in cytosolic Ca2+ levels observed during G1, starvation and meiosis, switches light chain preference to favor the recruitment of a single molecule of the calcium-insensitive calmodulin-like Cam2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on calcium levels, phosphorylation, and Cam2 binding.

claim: Phosphorylation of Myo1S742 is likely to impact Cam2 binding at the 1st IQ position.
source: However, it is worth noting that there are currently differences of opinion on the relationship between levels of Gad8 activity and cytosolic calcium (Cohen et al., 2014). The structures of the IQ region of Myosin-1 and calmodulin (Lu et al., 2015) suggest that phosphorylation of Myo1S742 is likely to impact Cam2 binding at the 1st IQ position.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural considerations and citation to Lu et al., 2015.

claim: Occupancy of IQ1 is required before a second CaM can bind to IQ2 (i.e. regulatory cooperative binding occurs).
source: Furthermore, our data reveal that CaM is unable to associate with IQ2 alone, as occupancy of IQ1 is required before a second CaM can bind to IQ2 (i.e. regulatory cooperative binding occurs).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental binding data.

claim: The switch in light-chain occupancy may provide a mechanism to change the stiffness of the Myo1 neck region and might thereby modulate the movement and force that is produced by this region during the acto-myosin ATPase cycle.
source: This switch in light-chain occupancy may provide a mechanism to change the stiffness of the Myo1 neck region (i.e. the 'lever arm') and might thereby modulate the movement and force that is produced by this region during the acto-myosin ATPase cycle and/or the load-sensitivity of its actin-bound form.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: Motor activity from a ring of myosins at the lip of the endosome is necessary for endocytic internalization.
source: Observations within budding yeast indicate that motor activity from a ring of myosins at the lip of the endosome (Mund et al., 2018) is necessary for endocytic internalization, but the mechanism by which the myosin interacts with actin to facilitate this localized activation is unknown (Sun et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mund et al., 2018 and Sun et al., 2006.

claim: The size of the early endocytic patch determines the number of Myo1 molecules necessary to generate a critical local concentration of Arp2/3-nucleated actin filaments.
source: Here we find that the size of the early endocytic patch determines the number of Myo1 molecules necessary to generate a critical local concentration of Arp2/3-nucleated actin filaments (Barker et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and citation to Barker et al., 2007.

claim: Myo1 is primed to act as a tension sensor against the actin filament as it pushes against the membrane of the internalized endosome and grows against the significant 0.85 MPa (8.3 atm) turgor pressure within the cell.
source: The Myo1 is then primed to act as a tension sensor against the actin filament as it pushes against the membrane of the internalized endosome and grows against the significant 0.85 MPa (8.3 atm) turgor pressure within the cell (Minc et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data and citation to Minc et al., 2009.

claim: The number of Myo1 molecules at the plasma membrane focus remains constant as the membrane is internalized until 2 s after Cam1 disassociates from Myo1.
source: The number of Myo1 molecules at the plasma membrane focus remains constant as the membrane is internalized until 2 s after Cam1 disassociates from Myo1.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the experimental TIRF imaging data.

claim: The trigger for Cam1 release is unknown, but the speed at which the event takes place indicates that it is likely to be initiated by a rapid localized spike in calcium.
source: The trigger for Cam1 release is unknown, but the speed at which the event takes place indicates that it is likely to be initiated by a rapid localized spike in calcium. This could perhaps be driven by a critical level of membrane deformation coupled to calcium influx, similar to processes proposed for mechano-transduction and the role of mammalian myosin-1 within the stereocilia of the inner ear (Adamek et al., 2008; Batters et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed based on the kinetics and citations to Adamek et al., 2008 and Batters et al., 2004.

claim: Once Cam1 detaches from the Myo1 molecule, the neck loses rigidity, reducing tension between the myosin motor and the actin filament, to promote detachment from F-actin.
source: Once Cam1 detaches from the Myo1 molecule, the neck loses rigidity, reducing tension between the myosin motor and the actin filament, to promote detachment from F-actin (Lewis et al., 2012; Mentes et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on citations to Lewis et al., 2012 and Mentes et al., 2018.

claim: Without an interaction with actin, Myo1 would leave the endocytic patch a second or so after losing its Cam1 light chain.
source: Single molecules of Myo1 do not reside for long at the plasma membrane (off rate is ~8 sec−1, Video 1), so without an interaction with actin, Myo1 would leave the endocytic patch a second or so after losing its Cam1 light chain.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the single-molecule kinetics data.

claim: The conformation and rigidity of the Myo1 lever arm play a key role in modulating the tension-sensing properties of the motor domain.
source: The conformation and rigidity of the Myo1 lever arm therefore play a key role in modulating the tension-sensing properties of the motor domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on lever arm conformation and dynamics.

claim: Phosphorylation-dependent changes in the conformation of the myosin neck provide a simple mechanism to modulate the rate of endocytosis according to the size and needs of the cell.
source: Phosphorylation-dependent changes in the conformation of the myosin neck provide a simple mechanism to modulate the rate of endocytosis according to the size and needs of the cell.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data.

claim: In the presence of Ca2+ and Myo1S742 phosphorylation, a single Cam2 resides at the IQ1 motif of the neck.
source: Similarly, in the presence of Ca2+ and Myo1S742 phosphorylation, a single Cam2 resides at the IQ1 motif of the neck (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental binding data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: A vacant IQ2 motif allows flexibility within the carboxyl half of the neck region, providing a relatively tension-insensitive motor that stalls against the actin polymer.
source: While bringing about a change in the conformation of the first half of the myosin lever arm (adjacent to the motor domain), the vacant IQ2 motif allows flexibility within the carboxyl half of the neck region. This would provide a relatively tension-insensitive motor that stalls against the actin polymer, which would therefore persist significantly longer at the endocytic foci, as observed to occur here in meiotic cells (Figure 8D, Supplementary file 1 Table 1).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data shown in Figure 8D and Supplementary file 1 Table 1.

claim: Phosphorylation-dependent changes in the calcium-regulated conformation and rigidity of the myosin lever arm could provide a universal mechanism for regulating the diverse cytoplasmic activities and functions of myosin motors within all cells.
source: Thus, phosphorylation-dependent changes in the calcium-regulated conformation and rigidity of the myosin lever arm could provide a universal mechanism for regulating the diverse cytoplasmic activities and functions of myosin motors within all cells.
evidence: This is a speculative generalization of the findings to other systems.
